purpose: Freeze the current external comparator versions and state their appropriate problem boundaries. This is a benchmark planning lock, not a claim that any comparison has been run.

comparators.name: NLR System Advisor Model
comparators.artifact: SAM
role: PV plant modeling
PV-battery and battery manual dispatch
CSP
geothermal plant model
important_limits: SAM does not provide a standalone battery CLI model; a battery can be evaluated through Generic System with plant losses configured appropriately.
SAM includes voltage, temperature and degradation detail not present in the simplified Symthaea grid-physics Battery model.
Only variables and boundaries that can be mapped exactly may enter differential validation.
comparators.pin_policy: Record installer/build identifier, SSC version, exact SAM case file, inputs, system configuration and output channel names.

comparators.name: REopt
comparators.artifact: REopt API / REopt.jl
comparators.pinned_release: API v3 stable; REopt.jl package/commit must be pinned per run
role: distributed energy resource sizing
facility/campus/community microgrid optimization
resilience and techno-economic assessment
important_limits: REopt API v3 uses REopt.jl as its optimization engine.
A short-horizon dispatch-only oracle is not comparable to a full technology-sizing/resilience run unless system boundary, costs, incentives, outage windows and objective are matched.
comparators.pin_policy: Record API route version, REopt.jl exact package version and manifest, optimizer/version, complete request JSON, response JSON and solve status.

comparators.name: PyPSA
comparators.artifact: PyPSA
role: multi-carrier energy system optimization
economic dispatch and unit commitment
network-constrained linear OPF
rolling-horizon and stochastic planning
capacity expansion
important_limits: PyPSA 1.4.0 includes correctness fixes to rolling-horizon unit commitment and security-constrained optimization; these behavior changes make the exact version important.
PyPSA 1.3.0 introduced piecewise-linear cost and efficiency curves and maintenance scheduling; verify exact availability and configuration at the selected release.
A linear or DC network formulation is not AC-OPF and must be labelled separately.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin PyPSA v1.4.0, Python/environment lock, Linopy and solver versions, network snapshot hashes, time weights, network formulation and all custom constraints.

comparators.name: GenX
comparators.artifact: GenX.jl
role: long-run electricity capacity expansion
generation and storage planning
transmission and operational planning
important_limits: The GitHub release list exposed v0.4.5 as the latest published release during this check; the repository README refers to v0.4.6. Pin the actual release tag/commit and do not assume main-branch code and released package are interchangeable.
GenX is a planning model, not a substitute for detailed component physics or project-specific site validation.
comparators.pin_policy: Use the immutable v0.4.5 tag/commit for a baseline; separately record any v0.4.6 development-branch run as unreleased.

comparators.name: NLR Annual Technology Baseline
comparators.artifact: NLR ATB Electricity
comparators.pinned_release: 2025 edition (latest published edition confirmed in this check; recheck before execution)
role: technology cost and performance assumptions
PV, wind, CSP, geothermal, hydropower, storage and hybrid system reference ranges
important_limits: The 2025 utility battery ATB includes LFP systems with 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 hour durations for a 60 MW reference system, based on bottom-up pack, inverter and balance-of-system costs.
ATB values are standardized U.S. reference assumptions; they must not be transferred directly to South Africa without local currency, financing, supply chain, tax, grid and construction adjustments.
comparators.pin_policy: Capture the exact technology page, scenario, financial assumptions, currency/base year, system size and downloaded data file.

comparators.name: PGLib-OPF
comparators.artifact: Power Grid Library — Optimal Power Flow
comparators.companion_engine: MATPOWER / PowerModels.jl or another pinned reference implementation
role: network optimal power flow
AC-OPF and declared DC-OPF cases
small network feasibility and solver comparison
important_limits: The library cases were curated primarily for AC-OPF; a DC formulation is a separate benchmark and must be declared.
Solver optimality status, non-convex local optimum and global certificate are distinct claims.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin immutable repository commit, exact case files, parser, per-unit/base-MVA mapping, solver and tolerances.

comparators.name: IEC PV monitoring
role: PV monitoring measurement classes
performance monitoring and analysis
soiling and bifacial monitoring
important_limits: Edition 3.0 is under development with forecast publication date 2027-07-30; do not describe it as an approved published standard as of this lock.
comparators.pin_policy: Record edition, corrigenda, monitoring class, sensor calibration and the exact measurement plan.

comparators.name: IEC wind power performance
role: single turbine power performance measurement
small wind turbine measurement
uncertainty in measured power curves and derived energy production
important_limits: A modelled wind atlas or generic turbine curve is not a measured IEC power-performance test.
comparators.pin_policy: Record edition, corrigenda, turbine configuration, met mast/lidar data, site calibration, uncertainty budget and test campaign.

comparators.name: South African Wholesale Electricity Market Code
comparators.artifact: SAWEM Market Code
role: wholesale trading and settlement rule context
market participation and balance responsibility assumptions
important_limits: A market-code document does not itself prove operational market readiness, participant registration, creditworthiness or any project's dispatch/settlement access.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin Market Code Rev 2.3 and the applicable Rule 1-4 documents; record legal effective status and operator licensing dependencies before modelling market participation.

comparators.name: IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs
comparators.artifact: Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2025
role: global renewable plant-level LCOE reference
global cost/performance trend baseline
important_limits: Global weighted-average LCOE values are plant-boundary cost comparisons, not a like-for-like firm-delivered electricity or grid-integration comparison.

IRENA notes that LCOE omits transmission and distribution expenditures beyond plant boundaries, assumes generation at maximum load factor, and does not capture the full economic value of dispatchability.
Global weighted averages are not South African project costs; do not transfer them without local financing, tax, labour, logistics, grid and resource adjustments.
comparators.context: IRENA states that more than 90% of utility-scale renewable projects commissioned in 2025 delivered power below the cost of the cheapest new fossil-fuel plant built in their market.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the report PDF and annex/database release, source date, commissioning cohort, 2025 USD basis and exact technology/boundary definition. Keep plant-gate values separate from delivered-service, storage, transmission and resilience costs.

comparators.name: ETHOS.RESKit
comparators.artifact: ETHOS.RESKit global wind-power workflow
comparators.pinned_release: Paper-specific archive: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17668776 (2025); current RESKit code release v0.5.0 (2026-07-10)
comparators.companion_engine: Python; pin exact archived paper environment separately from the current toolkit release
role: global onshore/offshore wind power time-series modelling
GWA4 and ERA5 wind-speed bias calibration
turbine configuration and power-curve comparison
wind-power model-to-observation validation

paper_reported_results.mast_calibration: 213 global mast locations across 25 countries; over 8 million filtered hourly measurements; paper states South Africa is among the geographic regions with mast observations
paper_reported_results.turbine_power_validation: More than 8 million hours from 152 turbine/wind-farm measurement sites; raw records are restricted by third-party agreements

hourly_capacity_factor_validation.cohort_note: Paper Table 2; calibrated hourly turbine/farm capacity-factor comparison. Non-calibrated relative mean error is reported as 0.292.

country_aggregate_validation.cohort: IEA country-level capacity/generation statistics, 2017-2021; up to 71 countries and offshore regions, with data gaps especially in Africa
country_aggregate_validation.main_text_global_capacity_factor: Model 0.287 versus IEA 0.306; main text reports 6.2% relative deviation and 23.1% for the non-calibrated workflow
country_aggregate_validation.abstract_note: The abstract separately states a 0.6% mean error for annual aggregate energy output; do not merge this with the main-text capacity-factor deviation without reproducing the exact metric and denominator.

important_limits: South African meteorological mast observations occur in the study's wider mast calibration geography, but the accessible article does not provide the exact site/record crosswalk needed to determine overlap for a new local holdout.
Do not use a South African WASA mast as a blind validation site until the exact mast ID, dates, heights and data overlap with the 213-mast calibration cohort are resolved.

Turbine/farm power validation is a separate dataset. The paper does not establish South African turbine-generation holdout validation; the raw power time series are restricted by third-party agreements.
The proprietary wind-farm inventory cannot be redistributed; it is obtained under a commercial licence.

The authors state the workflow is better suited to larger-scale assessments than exact single locations because ERA5/GWA4 cannot fully represent local wind conditions; diurnal, seasonal and terrain-based biases remain outside the presented correction method.
The abstract's annual aggregate 0.6% mean error is not the same metric as the detailed main-text global capacity-factor deviation (6.2%); preserve exact cohort, denominator and formula.
The current RESKit v0.5.0 release is not automatically identical to the paper-specific Zenodo archive. Pin and benchmark them separately.
comparators.pin_policy: For paper reproduction, pin Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.17668776 and its exact archived files/checksums. For a current software comparator, pin immutable Git tag v0.5.0 commit b41cf859fd619c5be717af84db5502b0ac4ca3e5, Python environment lock, GWA4/ERA5 inputs, turbine-library version, correction factors and exact metric cohort.

comparators.name: South African Hydropower Atlas
comparators.artifact: WRC Report TT 916/23 and SAHA ArcGIS E-Tool
comparators.pinned_release: Report TT 916/23, June 2023; E-Tool catalogue published 2022
role: South African hydropower site-discovery baseline
conduit/PRS, run-of-river, hydrokinetic, weir, WTW/WWTW and pumped-storage screening taxonomy
important_limits: The atlas is a South African discovery/pre-feasibility reference, not a bankable project register or measured site-data archive.
Initial criteria for several types were assumed because detailed data are limited; WWTW/WTW methods explicitly relied on assumptions.
Hydrokinetic South African case studies were scarce and flow estimates may diverge substantially from actual flow.
The 31,000 MW pumped-storage estimate is based on a 12-hour/day assumption and overlapping site pairs; the report states actual potential is significantly lower.
Geological, hydrological and environmental feasibility is not established for the identified pumped-storage candidates.
Do not compare a theoretical atlas estimate with a turbine test, metered generation or connected project capacity.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the report PDF bytes and SHA-256, E-Tool ArcGIS item IDs, each feature/raster service ID, original layer owner, CRS, resolution, data periods and rights. Treat report-derived estimates and actual feature data separately.

comparators.name: Water-distribution-network hydropower technology review
role: PAT and in-pipe turbine technology landscape
water-distribution energy recovery architectures
pressure regulation and off-grid telemetry energy harvesting context
important_limits: This is a literature review, not an independent performance test of a specific South African installation.
Its 40–75% broad PAT/micro-hydro efficiency range is not a universal design curve; use exact manufacturer maps or measured tests.
The review notes variable flow/head and service preservation issues; a fixed operating point is not representative.
Small harvested power may be more useful for off-grid sensors than grid export; evaluate those service boundaries separately.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the article version, DOI, PDF checksum, exact table/section and underlying primary source for any quantitative statement; do not treat cited case studies as raw reusable observations.

comparators.name: IEC pumped-storage hydropower trends
comparators.artifact: The future of pumped storage hydropower — Technology innovation and standardization trends (2025-2035)
role: pumped-storage technology and standardization trend context
technology and interoperability research horizon
important_limits: This is a trend report, not a component design standard, project approval, measured plant benchmark or site feasibility dataset.
Pumped storage is a storage asset: pumping input, generating output and round-trip losses must be kept separate from primary hydropower generation.
Do not use global deployment trends as a substitute for South African reservoir, geology, water rights or environmental assessment.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin IEC publication identifier 115300, report edition/date and exact pages for each technical trend. Apply actual published standards separately for design/acceptance.

comparators.name: International Hydropower Association World Hydropower Outlook
comparators.artifact: 2026 World Hydropower Outlook
role: global hydropower and pumped-storage deployment context
global market and development-pipeline trend comparison
important_limits: IHA database aggregates global industry development information; it is not a South African site-resource assessment.
Distinguish operating capacity, additions commissioned in the reporting year, projects under construction and the wider development pipeline.
Do not use pipeline capacity as an operating or bankable project.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the exact report PDF, database snapshot, geography, project status definition and reporting date.

comparators.name: DWS Water and Sanitation Sector Climate Response Strategy
comparators.artifact: Climate Change Response Strategy for Water and Sanitation Sector in South Africa
role: South African water/wastewater sector energy context
PAT and PRV energy recovery policy/sector precedent
important_limits: The report refers to PAT examples and pressure-reducing-valve recovery opportunities but is not an operating-site register or a metered performance database.
The document is copyright reserved; full acknowledgement is required and all figure/data reuse rights must be reviewed.
It does not establish the hydraulic profile, present status, measured output or owner consent of any specific site.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the official DWS PDF and exact pages, cite secondary claims only as context, and trace PAT examples to primary case studies/operator data before quantitative use.

comparators.name: IEC 60041 — hydraulic machine field acceptance
comparators.artifact: Field acceptance tests to determine the hydraulic performance of hydraulic turbines, storage pumps and pump-turbines
role: field acceptance test method for hydraulic turbine, storage pump and pump-turbine performance
contract-guarantee verification and uncertainty-aware field test reporting
important_limits: The standard defines test arrangements and calculation/reporting methods; it does not provide an unmeasured project's resource estimate, design approval or water-use authorisation.
A software trajectory is not a field acceptance test.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin IEC publication and corrigenda, exact test class, metrology, boundary, instrument calibration, uncertainty budget and test report.

comparators.name: IEC 60193 — hydraulic machine model acceptance
comparators.artifact: Hydraulic turbines, storage pumps and pump-turbines — Model acceptance tests
role: laboratory model acceptance and prototype-transposition test protocol for hydraulic machines
important_limits: Primary scope is models of machines above 5 MW unit power or 3 m reference diameter; application to smaller units is not generally justified except by agreement.
Does not replace field acceptance of an installed small-hydro unit or structural/mechanical qualification.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin edition, model geometry, test rig calibration, scale/transposition method and purchaser/supplier agreement where applied below normal scope.

comparators.name: IEC 61362 — hydraulic turbine governing systems
comparators.artifact: Guidelines to specification of hydraulic turbine governing systems
role: turbine governing-system specification and performance requirements
speed, power, water-level, opening/flow control and emergency shutdown specification
important_limits: This is a specification guideline, not an acceptance-test standard; acceptance procedures and guarantees are outside its scope.
Governing specification is not a complete water-service/surge safety case.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin edition and governing-system data sheets, actuator-energy provisions, emergency shutdown and required guarantee/test documents.

comparators.name: IEC 60545 — commissioning and operation
comparators.artifact: Guidelines for commissioning and operation of hydraulic turbines, pump-turbines and storage pumps
role: commissioning and operation procedures for hydraulic machines
operational test and machine handover context
important_limits: Commissioning and operation guidelines do not establish ongoing maintenance, site rights, ecological acceptability or project safety by themselves.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin edition and commissioning plan, tests, operational settings, machine configuration and handover record.

comparators.name: IEC 62006 — small hydro acceptance testing
comparators.artifact: Hydraulic machines — Acceptance tests of small hydroelectric installations
comparators.pinned_release: IEC 62006:2010 Edition 1.0 published; Edition 2 is a development project as of 2026-11-09
role: small-hydro field acceptance, safety approval, trial operation, reliability, cavitation/noise/vibration and performance verification
important_limits: IEC 62006:2010 applies to small hydro units up to about 15 MW and reference diameter around 3 m; it defines A/B/C acceptance test classes.
A second edition project is under development; do not claim that a draft or committee project is a published standard.
comparators.pin_policy: Use published IEC 62006:2010 for current test planning unless a formally published replacement is confirmed. Track Edition 2 project separately and recheck its publication status before use.

comparators.name: Open Water Analytics EPANET
comparators.artifact: OWA-EPANET network hydraulic analysis engine
comparators.pinned_release: v2.3.5; immutable tag commit 444725fbf16ab28b0470ef0ed281dc4849d49583; release published 2026-02-20
role: Current open-source distribution-network hydraulic baseline
Pressure-driven demand and FAVAD pressure-dependent leakage analysis
Multi-node pressure/flow, valve and network flow-balance simulation
important_limits: EPANET is a network hydraulic engine, not a native PAT electrical-conversion model or a certified transient water-hammer safety solver.

EPANET 2.3 introduced FAVAD pressure-dependent pipe leakage, a Positional Control Valve, independent pressure-unit support and a Flow Balance report; v2.3.5 is a patch release fixing flow-unit conversion for Generic curves and mixed-unit behavior.

Do not represent a PAT only as a PRV and call its electrical output physically validated. A calibrated hydraulic characteristic may be represented in the network only if it reproduces the declared PAT hydraulic boundary; electrical conversion remains a separate evidence-backed model.
No South African network site, leakage parameter or operating data is supplied by EPANET itself.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin OWA EPANET tag v2.3.5 and commit 444725fbf16ab28b0470ef0ed281dc4849d49583; record compiler/build flags, toolkit library digest, solver settings, units, input INP digest, demand/leakage/roughness parameters and complete report bytes.

comparators.name: Open Water Analytics EPANET historical replay
comparators.artifact: OWA-EPANET network hydraulic analysis engine for historical study reproduction
comparators.pinned_release: v2.2; immutable tag commit 4d8d82ddc260fce216af9321fc3d9a4646ac6827; release published 2019-12-10
role: Exact historical engine replay for the Cornubia 2022 PAT feasibility paper
Matched reproduction of EPANET 2.2 demand/pressure model behavior
important_limits: This is a historical reproduction pin, not the contemporary default engine.
The 2022 Cornubia paper explicitly used EPANET 2.2. Do not substitute 2.3.5 and label the result an exact reproduction.
The paper represented PAT sites through PRV proxies and calculated PAT energy separately; reproduction of that method must preserve its limitations.
The original Cornubia network data and rights must be independently resolved before claiming exact reproduction.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin OWA EPANET tag v2.2 and commit 4d8d82ddc260fce216af9321fc3d9a4646ac6827; bind the original Cornubia study network, inputs, controls, demand profiles and every annualization assumption before a result can be called reproduced.

comparators.name: Cornubia PAT feasibility study
comparators.artifact: Feasibility Analysis of Energy Recovery Using PATs in Water Distribution Networks
role: South African water-distribution PAT placement baseline
Matched Cornubia network pressure/leakage/energy model reproduction
important_limits: Five proposed PATs are modelled at 166.31 kW total candidate power; estimated leakage savings are 45.59 kL/month (18.16%). These are simulation outputs, not measured plant performance.
The paper used PRV proxies within EPANET 2.2 because the engine did not accurately model PAT components, then calculated output using pressure-drop/flow and empirical BEP assumptions.
Assumed operating windows (12 hours/day and 335 days/year) must be preserved during exact reproduction.
The network model and input data are not automatically open/redistributable just because the article is CC BY 4.0.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the exact article/PDF, EPANET 2.2 commit, full network input, demand chronology, PAT pump curves/BEP equations, pressure target, PAT operating hours and leakage model. Preserve all assumptions in the report.

comparators.name: UKZN PRV/PAT network optimization dissertation
comparators.artifact: Development of an automation model for leakage reduction and energy harnessing through optimised placement and setting of PRVs and PATs in WDNs
role: South African Cornubia and Pat Marshal PRV/PAT siting and settings comparator
Leakage-reduction and candidate PAT power model reproduction
important_limits: Reported Cornubia and Pat Marshal capacities and annual energy are modelled estimates, not metered electricity.
Cornubia overlaps the 2022 peer-reviewed Cornubia study; the two must not be treated as independent replications until network geometry, demand and candidate sites are crosswalked.
Public repository rights are stated as all rights reserved unless otherwise indicated; do not redistribute the dissertation or extract fixtures without permission.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin repository item 56056829-50d7-4258-b11e-e93233126edf, exact PDF and checksum, MATLAB/EPANET versions, network models, demand profiles, optimization setup and annualization assumptions.

comparators.name: Jowitt WDN PAT pressure-management study
comparators.artifact: Pressure management and energy production approaches in urban water distribution networks using pumps as turbines
comparators.companion_engine: Jowitt benchmark WDN; DDA and PDA extended-period simulations
role: PAT count/placement and discharge-selection strategy comparison
Demand-driven versus pressure-driven WDN method comparison
Leakage-pressure-energy trade-off comparator
important_limits: The study uses the Jowitt benchmark network, not a South African utility network.
Its reported one-to-five PAT energy totals differ between DDA and PDA; exact units, periods, scenarios and assumptions must be retained.
The article reports higher leakage reduction and lower pressures for PRVs in the tested configurations, so energy and water-loss results must remain separate.
Data are available on request rather than as a public matched validation corpus.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin article/PDF, exact Jowitt network data and demand pattern, PAT model, DDA/PDA settings, 24-hour horizon, PAT count, discharge selection and reported metric definitions.

comparators.name: Multi-node PAT real-time control
comparators.artifact: Multi-Node real time control for pressure regulation and energy recovery in WDNs using Pump-as-Turbines
comparators.pinned_release: Control Engineering Practice 169, April 2026, Article 106777; DOI 10.1016/j.conengprac.2026.106777
comparators.companion_engine: Pressure-driven unsteady-flow model; Kalman filter + tracking MPC + PAT actuator-settings optimiser
role: Current multi-node PAT pressure-control research comparator
Kalman state/disturbance estimation and tracking MPC benchmark
Coordinated pressure and energy-recovery controller method
important_limits: Reported results are closed-loop simulations, not a field controller deployment.
The article uses an existing WDN and pressure-driven unsteady-flow model; do not compare its network controller directly with a one-conduit steady-state power calculator.
No South African field validation is established by the paper.
A controller method does not confer OT write authority, operational approval or water-service safety certification.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the exact paper/PDF, supplementary files, network/measurement data and method implementation; reproduce the Kalman filter, multi-output tracking MPC and actuator-settings optimiser before numerical comparison.

comparators.name: EPANET-RS native Rust hydraulic solver
comparators.artifact: epanet-rs hydraulic solver reimplementation
role: Experimental Rust hydraulic engine for differential parity
Possible parallel Monte Carlo scenario solver
important_limits: Upstream describes numerical parity as a design goal, not a completed independent qualification.
Upstream claims up to 5x parallel speedup only for supported extended-period networks without tanks or controls; reproduce on identical inputs.
The 0.2.3 feature checklist marks leakage, rules, energy and quality as not implemented. Do not substitute for OWA where pipe leakage/FAVAD is required.
The API is described as partially compatible with OWA. Unsupported cases must fall back to the reference solver.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin exact crates.io version and Cargo.lock checksum; separately record the inspected source revision and the OWA reference commit. Retain the same INP inputs and options for differential comparison.

comparators.name: Rust safe OWA EPANET API wrapper
comparators.artifact: epanet 0.3.0 safe Rust wrapper around the OWA EPANET 2.3 C API
role: Safe Rust interface to the official OWA EPANET C engine
Extended-period hydraulic simulation and node/link result retrieval
important_limits: This wraps the OWA C solver; it is not an independent hydraulic solver.
The EPANET project handle is Send but not Sync; a project instance requires synchronization for shared concurrent access.
The lower-level epanet-sys crate builds the C submodule with CMake and bindgen and requires a C compiler and libclang.
Cross-platform builds and exact compatibility with the pinned 2.3.5 source must be verified.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin epanet 0.3.0 and transitive dependencies; pin exact OWA EPANET C engine tag/commit, native build configuration and platform binary/source digests.

comparators.name: Antalya full-scale PAT water-network operation
comparators.artifact: Evaluation of performance and environmental benefits of a full-scale pump as turbine system in Antalya water distribution network
role: full-scale PAT/PRV bypass field operation
online flow, pressure and power monitoring
real-world pressure management and energy recovery
important_limits: Initial operational evidence covers approximately five months, not multi-year fleet reliability.

Published abstract reports 130–300 m3/h and 0.7–8.4 kWh for about 100 kPa pressure reduction, but the abstract does not state the energy interval; do not convert to kW or annual energy without the full paper.
Average efficiency 60% and 53-day / 1.8-month payback are case-specific; payback uses study financial/environmental assumptions.
2017 ASCE publication DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)WR.1943-5452.0000795 describes the same Antalya installation; do not treat it as an independent second plant.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the IWA Water Supply article, exact operational period, SCADA sampling interval, PAT/PRV topology, meter boundaries, uncertainty and any supplementary time series. Link the 2017 ASCE paper to the same installation identity.

comparators.name: Manservigi et al. PAT regulation and 16 experimental turbomachine maps
comparators.artifact: Hydraulic and electrical regulations of pumps as turbines for energy recovery in water distribution networks: Energy and economic analysis
comparators.pinned_release: Cambridge Prisms: Water; published online 2025-06-16; DOI 10.1017/wat.2025.10004
role: experimental PAT curves for 16 turbomachines
hydraulic versus electrical regulation comparison
real-world WDN techno-economic selection
important_limits: The 16 machine characteristic curves are experimental component evidence; the Northern Italy WDN integration is a model/case evaluation, not 16 commissioned field PATs.
The network serves approximately 5,000 users in Northern Italy and is not a South African validation site.

The paper reports 44.1% of available network hydraulic energy recoverable for its selected candidate, maximum investment €24,500, LCOE €74–180/MWh for hydraulic regulation and €269/MWh for electrical regulation under its case assumptions.
Electrical regulation bypasses the selected PAT in 72.4% of cases in the reported scenario; hydraulic/electrical operating policy and bypass losses materially affect recovery.
Article reuse licence is CC BY-NC; non-commercial reuse only, with commercial permission required.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin article PDF/DOI, the exact 16 turbine-mode characteristic curves, measurement boundary and uncertainty. Reproduce the case study separately from the experimental curves; preserve non-commercial licence restrictions.

comparators.name: Pugliese et al. PAT test-rig characterization
comparators.artifact: Experimental characterization of two Pumps As Turbines for hydropower generation
role: laboratory characterization of two pumps in turbine mode
comparison of experimental PAT curves to theoretical pump-to-turbine conversion models
important_limits: Only two pump configurations are described in the abstract; no universal pump-to-turbine conversion curve follows.
The paper notes the lack of manufacturer reverse-mode information and limited laboratory campaigns as an unresolved prediction problem.
Exact maps, test uncertainty and operating domains require full-paper data extraction.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin exact pump identities, test-rig geometry, head, flow, rotational speed, torque/power, test uncertainty and original characteristic-curve tables before using the data.

comparators.name: Parra et al. intelligent PAT/PRV pressure-control experiment
comparators.artifact: Intelligent pressure management by pumps as turbines in water distribution systems: results of experimentation
role: laboratory PAT+PRV pressure modulation under variable discharge
critical-node pressure tracking
comparison with conventional PRV water-saving baseline
important_limits: Study combines hydraulic modelling and extensive experimentation for a German case; it is not a South African full-scale field trial.
2.3 kW is reported as a full-load maximum and 40% as maximum total net system efficiency; neither should be treated as sustained average output.
The up-to-16% water savings are relative to the tested conventional PRV setup and demand profile, not a universal leakage reduction.
Seasonal flow/pressure variability, investment and operational suitability require site-level analysis.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the full article/supplement, PAT model, variable-discharge test sequence, critical-point pressure target, flow/power metrology and exact net-system efficiency boundary.

comparators.name: WRC Queenswood PAT pilot — measured point observations
comparators.artifact: A High Level Scoping Investigation into the Potential of Energy Saving and Production/Generation in the Supply of Water Through Pressurised Conduits
role: South African PAT pilot point-measurement reference
Queenswood measured flow/head/electrical output known-point reconstruction
important_limits: Report Table i contains five time-stamped observations, with measured output 2.323–4.521 kW at 27.55–32.49 L/s and 25.04–30.94 m reported head drops.
Only five point observations; no continuous duty cycle, seasonal availability or annual generation evidence.
The report describes the pilot as not optimized; reverse-mode characteristics were estimated/provided by the pump manufacturer rather than established as a fully characterized PAT map.
The 2014 Tshwane article describes this same Queenswood installation; it is not a second independent field installation.
One WRC table heading uses 'energy' where the reported values are watts; preserve measured power units and do not reinterpret as kWh.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the WRC report PDF and Table i; recover raw test logs, meter calibration, time intervals, sensor locations and exact head boundary from the University of Pretoria/Tshwane custodians. Keep the 2014 Queenswood citation linked to this same installation ID.

comparators.name: Tshwane Pierre van Ryneveld 15 kW conduit hydro pilot
comparators.artifact: Conduit-hydropower potential in the City of Tshwane water distribution system: A discussion of potential applications, financial and other benefits
comparators.pinned_release: Journal of the South African Institution of Civil Engineering, Vol. 56 No. 3, October 2014
role: South African municipal conduit-hydropower installation
Cross-flow turbine / synchronous generator on existing water supply infrastructure
Generator frequency/load rejection/PRV response fault-case evidence
important_limits: The paper documents three field experiments and a 29 November 2011 launch, with a cross-flow turbine and synchronous generator; approximately 15 kW is a maximum capacity depending on head/flow, not an annual average.
Queenswood and Pierre van Ryneveld are distinct installations; Queenswood is the WRC KV 238/10 pilot and must not be double counted.
Authors report generator frequency control, load rejection, PRV hunting, variable water supply and manual operation as issues requiring improvement.
National/Tshwane theoretical MWh figures are preliminary screening potential, not measured output.
Current operating status and raw multi-year power/flow data are not established.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the SciELO article, exact site identity, three experiment conditions and launch evidence. Obtain the original Tshwane operational logs and permission before using any telemetry.

comparators.name: Drakenstein Leliefontein bidirectional municipal PAT station
comparators.artifact: Leliefontein Pump-As-Turbine Station
comparators.companion_engine: SCADA + bidirectional power meter + active-front-end variable-speed drives
role: South African bidirectional pump/PAT station
Grid import/export and SCADA instrumentation reference
Pumping-versus-generating net-energy accounting
important_limits: The paper reports the installation operating since June 2018, with bidirectional operation, active-front-end drives, actuated valves, grid protection, power metering and SCADA.
320 MWh/year and 9.9 GWh over 2018–2041 are estimates, not an admitted independently audited interval-meter series.

The paper also gives cumulative numbers of 271,236 MWh generated and 53,577 MWh consumed which are inconsistent with those annual/lifetime estimates; treat their units as unresolved and do not use as MWh without confirmation.
The station serves both pumping and generation roles; calculate net energy benefit after pumping consumption and parasitic loads.
Raw SCADA/meter exports, calibration, sample intervals and current operating status are not supplied in the paper.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin the IMESA paper, request Drakenstein SCADA and bidirectional-meter exports with calibration certificates, import/export registers, timestamp granularity and pump/turbine mode status. Resolve the conflicting cumulative units with the authors/municipality before benchmarking.

comparators.name: South African low-enthalpy geothermal prospectivity study
comparators.artifact: South Africa's geothermal energy hotspots inferred from subsurface temperature and geology
comparators.pinned_release: South African Journal of Science 113(11/12), 2017; DOI 10.17159/sajs.2017/20170092
role: South African geothermal geology and low-enthalpy prospectivity context
Geothermal exploration evidence gap baseline
important_limits: The study combines available subsurface temperature and heat-flow measurements with solute geothermometry and geology; it is not a proven power reservoir.
The paper explicitly calls for new temperature measurements and structural, hydrogeological and economic investigations.
Low-enthalpy direct heat is not the same use case as high-temperature electricity generation.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin article and underlying observation references, well depths, temperature measurements, geochemistry, date and uncertainty. Preserve regional prospectivity as an exploration lead, not proven reserve.

comparators.name: South African marine renewable resource and spatial-planning context
comparators.artifact: Marine Spatial Planning National Data: Uses and Interests — Marine Renewable Energy
comparators.pinned_release: DFFE marine spatial planning report, section 3.7.4; published circa 2021
role: South African wave/current/offshore wind/OTEC resource context
Tidal-range suitability negative control
Marine spatial planning and consent context
important_limits: The report cites theoretical coastal wave power locally up to 100 kW/m; this is not device-captured energy or P90 yield.
It states that South African tidal ranges are too small for appreciable tidal-range power; this is distinct from Agulhas Current extraction and wave energy.
It says early assessment had not identified project-ready sites and flags local industry, cost and regulatory uncertainty.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin report version, spatial layers and underlying measurement/hindcast sources; do not treat national-scale resource statements as a project site or environmental permit.

comparators.name: Fervo Cape Station GeoBlock 1 commercial EGS operation
comparators.artifact: Fervo Energy Q3 2026 results and Cape Station GeoBlock 1 commercial-operation milestone
comparators.pinned_release: Company Q3 2026 release published 2026-11-09; GeoBlock 1 COD 2026-09-30
role: Current commercial EGS deployment comparator
33 MW net GeoBlock commercial operation and PPA delivery reference
important_limits: The 33 MW net output and status are company-reported; public release does not include raw third-party-audited interval meter data.
A 396 MW future Google offtake and optional expansion are future delivery commitments, not currently operating capacity.
Utah geothermal, permitting, drilling supply chain, financing and PPA context do not transfer to South Africa.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin company release and date. Independently obtain net meter series, availability, parasitic loads, wellfield decline, drilling and surface plant costs before treating results as verified operating performance.

comparators.name: Geothermal global experience-rate dataset and cost-learning analysis
comparators.artifact: Experience rates of current and future geothermal power technologies
role: Geothermal historical cost-learning comparator
Hydrothermal vs EGS/closed-loop evidence boundary
important_limits: Global hydrothermal experience rate of approximately -20% is a historical study result, not a forecast for every geothermal project.
Country experience rates vary substantially; global averages can hide local learning and institutional differences.
EGS and closed-loop technologies have much shorter commercial histories and weaker cost-learning evidence.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin source dataset and cost-normalization methods; retain country and technology classes separately. Treat EGS/closed-loop cost trajectories as uncertain, not a direct continuation of hydrothermal history.

comparators.name: Perovskite-silicon tandem manufacturing and stability research
comparators.artifact: Scalable ambient fabrication of single-junction and perovskite–silicon tandem solar cells
role: Advanced PV laboratory efficiency comparator
Ambient blade-coated process and early module-scale stability reference
important_limits: The paper reports a 33.0% certified tandem cell, 26.5% certified single-junction cell and 23.2% module; these are different device boundaries.
The 1,200-hour light-soaking retention is a laboratory condition, not a 25-year field warranty.
Factory yield, module area, throughput, capex, bankability, outdoor degradation and end-of-life lead management remain unresolved.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin article and supplementary data. Compare cell and module separately; require independent IEC/ISOS testing, scale yield, field degradation, encapsulation, lead containment and recycling before commercial product claims.

comparators.name: Low-head hydropower full-scale validation gap review
comparators.artifact: Full-scale validation gaps and opportunities for low-head hydropower: a review and perspective
comparators.pinned_release: Sustainable Energy Technologies and Assessments 93, article 105218; September 2026
role: Low-head hydro technology validation and test-rig capability comparison
Retired/underused hydraulic infrastructure as potential full-scale test bed
important_limits: U.S. test-facility flow capability figures are a U.S. case study, not South African test-facility capability.
The article is a review/perspective, not a turbine test result or a site-specific resource study.
Fish passage, sediment continuity and water quality require independent field evidence.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin article, reviewed facility capability data and turbine classes. Perform a separate South African test-site access, head/flow, safety and environmental capability audit.

comparators.name: Shallow-water hydrokinetic design and validation review
comparators.artifact: Shallow-Water Hydrokinetic Turbines: A Critical Systematic Review of Design Parameters, Performance Validation, and Deployment Challenges
comparators.pinned_release: Journal of Sustainable Development of Energy, Water and Environment Systems 14(3), 2026; DOI 10.13044/j.sdewes.d14.0715
role: Hydrokinetic cross-flow and floating-water-wheel performance comparator
Laboratory-to-field scale-effect and uncertainty benchmark
important_limits: The reported 15–45% laboratory-to-field degradation applies to reviewed shallow-water hydrokinetic devices, not automatically to pressurized conduit PATs.
Cross-flow turbine power coefficients depend on blockage, depth and free-surface assumptions.
The review characterizes shallow-water hydrokinetics as niche in its reviewed market context, not a low-cost general substitute for solar.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin review and included device evidence. Keep power coefficient, head-based turbine efficiency and net electrical efficiency distinct; test field/scale derating for the exact product family.

comparators.name: Compressed-air energy storage and thermal integration review
comparators.artifact: Technologies and prospects for compressed air energy storage
role: Long-duration mechanical storage comparator
Adiabatic CAES / thermal-storage integration and part-load performance
important_limits: The 50–70% round-trip efficiency range is a broad review value dependent on system configuration, not a guarantee for a new project.
Geological reservoir, sealing, fatigue, thermal retention and compressor/expander part-load maps are site- and design-specific.
Do not compare storage-level USD/kWh with generator LCOE without duration, power, round-trip losses and delivered-service boundary.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin review and demonstration dataset; model compression, thermal storage, expansion, parasitics, pressure, cycling and seasonal standby on matched duty with other storage technologies.

comparators.name: European marine renewable levelized-cost and deployment comparator
comparators.artifact: Marine Renewable Energy — EU Blue Economy Observatory
comparators.pinned_release: European Commission Blue Economy Observatory page, updated 2026
role: Tidal-stream and wave LCOE market comparator
Marine technology commercial maturity and CfD reference
important_limits: Published European LCOE ranges are EUR 110–480/MWh for tidal stream and EUR 160–750/MWh for wave; these are broad European technology/project ranges, not South African costs.
Flowatt reference prices and UK CfD strike prices are jurisdiction-specific and include policy/contract context.
Marine technology LCOE is highly deployment-, resource-, survivability- and finance-dependent.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin page revision/date and the underlying IRENA/OceanSET/auction source definitions. Preserve EUR year, technology maturity, project scope and contract assumptions.

comparators.name: Oppelt et al. 2025 mine-water energy and monitoring review
comparators.artifact: Mine Water as an Energy Source: Overview of Technical Basics, Existing Plants, and Monitoring Results
comparators.pinned_release: Mine Water and the Environment 44, 519–543; published 2025-05-15; DOI 10.1007/s10230-025-01057-w
role: Mine-water heating/cooling technical architecture comparator
Mine-water renewal, pumping head, chemistry and nearby-consumer requirements
important_limits: Useful thermal energy depends on stable flow, mine-water renewal, temperature and consumer proximity; mine void volume alone is not a sustainable heat resource.
Pumping head, heat exchanger mineralization, reinjection temperature and chemistry can dominate system economics.
International case studies are not South African site validation.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin review version and original operating-plant case sources. Extract each case with its own system boundary, raw metering and uncertainty; do not pool reported COP or costs across different systems.

comparators.name: 2026 operating mine-water heating and feasibility case
comparators.artifact: Technical lessons learned from the usage of geothermal mine water for heat supply and economic scenarios to predict feasibility
comparators.pinned_release: Energy Conversion and Management 349, article 120809; 2026-02-01; DOI 10.1016/j.enconman.2025.120809
role: Operating mine-water heating case comparator
Heat-network loss and heat-exchanger mineralization benchmark
Economic sensitivity to energy and carbon prices
important_limits: The study reports 14–22-year amortization scenarios for its specific project assumptions; not a South African payback estimate.
Heat-network losses and mineralization are critical optimization issues in the case, but site-specific exchanger and chemistry behaviour differ.
The published abstract does not provide raw operator meter exports for an independent Luminous reproduction.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin complete paper, monitoring boundary, heat-meter and pumping measurements, chemistry, maintenance and scenario assumptions. Recompute economics for each South African site's tariffs and finance.

comparators.name: CSIR/SANEDI South African industrial thermal test capability
comparators.artifact: Supporting Industry with Thermal Systems
comparators.pinned_release: CSIR Energy Research Centre / SANEDI industrial thermal systems support programme
role: South African thermal test capability and collaboration lead
Industrial solar heat, heat pumps, thermal storage and waste-heat testing context
important_limits: The page describes existing and planned capability; planned facilities must not be represented as operational test rigs until confirmed.
No product qualification or full industrial site performance is established by the programme page.
comparators.pin_policy: Confirm current operating capability, instrument ranges, calibration, uncertainty, safety certification and available collaboration terms directly with CSIR/SANEDI.

comparators.name: GreenCape 2026 South African industrial heating alternatives
comparators.artifact: Decarbonising Industrial Heating: Evaluating Low-Carbon Alternatives for Industrial Thermal Systems
role: South African industrial process heat and steam context
LCOH, carbon liability and operational suitability comparison
important_limits: A sector brief is not a substitute for an individual plant's process temperature, duty, boiler efficiency, production continuity or fuel records.
Published cost and policy assumptions require site-specific tariff and financing updates.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin report and any underlying tables; construct a plant-level comparison using measured process heat profiles and include backup/production constraints.

comparators.name: High-temperature heat-pump technology and industrial applications
comparators.artifact: High-temperature heat pumps: key technologies and industrial applications toward carbon-neutral process heating
role: Industrial heat-pump cycle and working-fluid comparator
80–160°C process heat application and temperature-lift analysis
important_limits: Temperature ranges in the review are application context, not guaranteed unit performance.
COP depends on source/sink temperature, lift, refrigerant, compressor, part-load and auxiliary power.
A process heat project requires continuous duty and product-quality constraints, not just a rated outlet temperature.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin review version and underlying experimental maps. Compare on same source temperature, delivery temperature, thermal load chronology and system COP including auxiliaries.

comparators.name: Freiberg mine-water thermal storage pilot
comparators.artifact: Mine water heat storage with heat pump as a solution for decarbonisation in urban areas
role: Seasonal mine-water thermal storage pilot comparator
Long-duration heat/cooling storage and heat-pump integration
important_limits: The 45–65% storage-efficiency range and >2-year testing refer to one Freiberg mine pilot; not a universal mine thermal-storage efficiency.
Up-to-80% district self-sufficiency and >3-month duration are modelled district scenarios, not measured South African field service.
Mine-water temperature, replenishment and geology differ from South African mines.
comparators.pin_policy: Pin paper, raw pilot time series, storage efficiency formula, temperature/flow measurement boundary and model-vs-measured distinction.

comparators.name: Council for Geoscience mine-water and environmental-water management
comparators.artifact: Mine and Environmental Water Management Project
comparators.pinned_release: Council for Geoscience project page; no publication date stated
role: South African mine-water management source lead
Witwatersrand water ingress, pump-and-treat and acid mine drainage context
important_limits: The project page is water/environmental management context, not a thermal resource or mine-water heat potential dataset.
Mine-water containment, treatment and clean-water protection are primary; energy recovery is secondary and requires separate rights.
comparators.pin_policy: Obtain mine- and operator-specific data, water-use/ discharge approvals and environmental constraints; do not infer heat capacity from project location.
